```{r}
# every table gets a bold header row: kable writes a Markdown (pipe) table, whose first line is the header
kable <- function(...) {
  k <- knitr::kable(...)
  if (!identical(attr(k, "format"), "pipe")) return(k)
  cells <- strsplit(k[1], "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  bold <- function(x) {
    t <- trimws(x)
    if (t == "" || startsWith(t, "**") || startsWith(t, "\textbf{")) x else sub(t, paste0("**", t, "**"), x, fixed = TRUE)
  }
  k[1] <- paste(vapply(cells, bold, ""), collapse = "|")
  if (endsWith(attr(k, "format"), "pipe") && !endsWith(k[1], "|")) k[1] <- paste0(k[1], "|")
  k
}
```

```{r}
#| label: wm-calc
# Correspondence analysis of the nationality x word table: the three most specific words of each nationality,
# counted in every answer with a nationality of the seven models (analysis/word_map.py; no judge).
wm <- as.matrix(read.csv(file.path("..", "analysis", "out", "word_map_counts.csv"), row.names = 1,
                         check.names = FALSE))
P_ <- wm / sum(wm); rm_ <- rowSums(P_); cm_ <- colSums(P_)
sv_ <- svd(diag(1 / sqrt(rm_)) %*% (P_ - rm_ %o% cm_) %*% diag(1 / sqrt(cm_)))
ca_in <- 100 * sv_$d^2 / sum(sv_$d^2)
ca_row <- diag(1 / sqrt(rm_)) %*% sv_$u[, 1:2] %*% diag(sv_$d[1:2])
ca_col <- diag(1 / sqrt(cm_)) %*% sv_$v[, 1:2] %*% diag(sv_$d[1:2])
# orientation: origin and risk to the right, warmth at the top
s1_ <- sign(ca_row[rownames(wm) == "NGA", 1]); s2_ <- sign(ca_row[rownames(wm) == "ITA", 2])
ca_row <- ca_row %*% diag(c(s1_, s2_)); ca_col <- ca_col %*% diag(c(s1_, s2_))
w_idx <- inner_join(rate_table("defensive_marking") |> filter(country != "BASE") |>
                      group_by(country) |> summarise(def = mean(pct), .groups = "drop"),
                    rate_table("stereo_pos") |> filter(country != "BASE") |>
                      group_by(country) |> summarise(pos = mean(pct), .groups = "drop"), by = "country") |>
  mutate(idx = def - pos)
ramp <- scales::gradient_n_pal(c("#2a78d6", "#8a8780", "#e8452c"))
nat_pts <- tibble(country = rownames(wm), x = ca_row[, 1], y = ca_row[, 2]) |>
  left_join(w_idx, by = "country") |>
  mutate(lab = nm(country), col = ramp(scales::rescale(idx)), kind = "nat")
# the three families: Ward clustering of the nationalities on the two axes shown; a nationality whose
# silhouette is below 0.45 sits between two families and is left outside the outlines
fam_h <- hclust(dist(ca_row), "ward.D2")
fam_g <- cutree(fam_h, 3)
fam_sil <- cluster::silhouette(fam_g, dist(ca_row))[, "sil_width"]
fam_name <- setNames(c("warm", "reserved", "origin"),
                     c(fam_g[rownames(wm) == "ITA"], fam_g[rownames(wm) == "FIN"], fam_g[rownames(wm) == "NGA"]))
nat_pts <- nat_pts |> mutate(fam = unname(fam_name[as.character(fam_g)]), sil = fam_sil,
                             inside = sil >= 0.45)
between <- nat_pts$country[!nat_pts$inside]
FAM_COL <- c(warm = "#eda100", reserved = "#2a78d6", origin = "#e8452c")
# a word takes the colour of the nationality it is most over-used for (observed / expected count)
over_ <- wm / (rowSums(wm) %o% colSums(wm) / sum(wm))
word_pts <- tibble(lab = colnames(wm), x = ca_col[, 1], y = ca_col[, 2],
                   country = rownames(wm)[apply(over_, 2, which.max)]) |>
  mutate(col = nat_pts$col[match(country, nat_pts$country)], kind = "word")
# the carousel is in English only: the words of the map, translated from the French the AIs wrote
WORD_EN <- c(ambassade = "embassy", argent = "money", arnaque = "scam", art = "art", "autodérision" = "self-mockery",
             chaleur = "warmth", chaleureux = "warm", chocolat = "chocolate", "communauté" = "community",
             direct = "direct", "discrétion" = "discretion", "débat" = "debate", "décontracté" = "relaxed",
             enthousiasme = "enthusiasm", expressif = "expressive", famille = "family", femme = "women",
             franchise = "frankness", guerre = "war", harmonie = "harmony", histoire = "history", honneur = "honour",
             "hospitalité" = "hospitality", humour = "humour", intellectuel = "intellectual", ironie = "irony",
             nature = "nature", origine = "origin", "passionné" = "passionate", politesse = "politeness",
             "ponctualité" = "punctuality", pot = "a drink", pourboire = "tip", religion = "religion",
             respect = "respect", "réservé" = "reserved", silence = "silence", "simplicité" = "simplicity",
             sport = "sport", tradition = "tradition", traduction = "translation", urgence = "emergency",
             "égalitaire" = "egalitarian", "égalité" = "equality", "étranger" = "foreigner")
word_pts <- word_pts |> mutate(lab = coalesce(unname(WORD_EN[lab]), lab))
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 5.2
s_def <- rate_table("defensive_marking") |> select(model, country, def = pct)
s_pos <- rate_table("stereo_pos") |> select(model, country, pos = pct)
s_neg <- rate_table("negative_association") |> select(model, country, neg = k)
pm <- s_def |> inner_join(s_pos, by = c("model", "country")) |> inner_join(s_neg, by = c("model", "country"))
mid <- pm |> group_by(country) |>
  summarise(def = mean(def), pos = mean(pos), neg = sum(neg), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(lab = nm(country),
         lean = rank(def) - rank(pos))
nat <- mid |> filter(country != "BASE")
ctl <- mid |> filter(country == "BASE")
mx <- median(nat$def); my <- median(nat$pos)
XMAX <- 10 * ceiling(max(nat$def) / 10) + 18; YMAX <- 10 * ceiling(max(nat$pos) / 10) + 12  # more room than in the report: the chart is smaller here
ggplot(nat, aes(def, pos)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = mx, ymin = my, ymax = Inf, fill = "#2a78d6", alpha = 0.16) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = mx, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = my, fill = "#d63c2a", alpha = 0.16) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mx, linetype = "dashed", colour = GRID) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = my, linetype = "dashed", colour = GRID) +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = YMAX - 1, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, family = "Inter", fontface = "bold",
           size = 4.62, colour = "#2a78d6", label = "CULTURAL GUIDE") +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = YMAX - 4, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, family = "Inter", size = 3.64,
           colour = MUTED, label = "compliments, ice-breakers") +
  annotate("text", x = XMAX - 1, y = my - 1, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, family = "Inter", fontface = "bold",
           size = 4.62, colour = "#d63c2a", label = "SECURITY GUARD") +
  geom_point(aes(size = neg, fill = lean), shape = 21, colour = NIGHT, stroke = 0.6, alpha = 0.95) +
  geom_point(data = ctl, shape = 8, size = 4.20, colour = INK, stroke = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = ctl$def + 2, y = ctl$pos + 2.2, hjust = 0, family = "Inter", size = 3.64,
           colour = INK, label = "\"a man\" (no nationality)") +
  # point.size: the labels keep clear of the bubbles, whose area grows with the negative associations
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = lab, point.size = sqrt(neg / max(nat$neg)) * 11 + 1.8), family = "Inter",
                  size = 3.78, colour = INK, seed = 4,
                  point.padding = 0.3, box.padding = 0.35, min.segment.length = 0.3,
                  segment.colour = "#55585f", max.overlaps = 40, force = 3, ylim = c(NA, YMAX - 9)) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2a78d6", mid = "#b9b7b1", high = "#d63c2a", midpoint = 0, guide = "none") +
  scale_size(range = c(1.8, 11), limits = c(0, max(nat$neg)), breaks = c(0, 10, 30, 60),
             name = "answers linking him to a risk (seven AIs)") +
  guides(size = guide_legend(override.aes = list(fill = "#b9b7b1"))) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = \(x) paste0(x, " %"), limits = c(-1.5, XMAX), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = \(x) paste0(x, " %"), limits = c(-2, YMAX), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = "\"his origin does not matter\" (defensive marking)", y = "compliments on his culture") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```


```{r}
#| fig-height: 5.3
ISO2 <- c(FIN = "fi", JPN = "jp", AUS = "au", ITA = "it", SWE = "se", RUS = "ru", DZA = "dz", IND = "in",
          NGA = "ng", AFG = "af", FRA = "fr", BEL = "be", ESP = "es", CHE = "ch", GBR = "gb")
cmp <- sp_ |> arrange(desc(p)) |> mutate(rank = row_number(), lab = nm(country))
cmp5 <- bind_rows(head(cmp, 5), tail(cmp, 5)) |>
  mutate(grp = ifelse(rank <= 5, "most complimented", "least complimented"), lab = factor(lab, levels = rev(lab)))
ggplot(cmp5, aes(p, lab, fill = grp)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = pc(p)), hjust = -0.15, family = "Inter", fontface = "bold", size = 5, colour = INK) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("most complimented" = "#1baf7a", "least complimented" = "#d63c2a"),
                    breaks = c("most complimented", "least complimented")) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, max(cmp5$p) * 1.2), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = "answers with a compliment on his culture (mean of the 7 AIs)", y = NULL) +
  # each man's flag between his name and his bar (flags/png, drawn by flags/build.sh)
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(cmp5)), function(i) {
    f <- file.path("flags", "png", paste0(ISO2[[cmp5$country[i]]], ".png"))
    annotation_custom(grid::rasterGrob(png::readPNG(f), x = unit(-0.24, "in"), width = unit(0.33, "in"),
                                       height = unit(0.22, "in")),
                      xmin = 0, xmax = 0, ymin = as.integer(cmp5$lab[i]), ymax = as.integer(cmp5$lab[i]))
  }) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14, colour = INK),
        # invisible ticks as long as a flag leave it room between the name and the bar
        axis.ticks.y = element_line(colour = NA), axis.ticks.length.y = unit(0.46, "in"),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 11))
```

<!-- 8: the map of the world -->
```{r}
#| label: map-calc
# the families of the word map, on a world map: each nationality takes the colour of its family; Romania and
# Russia, whose silhouette is below 0.45, sit between two families
MAP_NAME <- c("United Kingdom" = "UK", "United States" = "USA")
fam_lab <- c(warm = "warm, passionate", reserved = "reserved, punctual", origin = "his origin, honour, war, scams",
             between = "in between")
map_fill <- c(FAM_COL, between = "#8a4a3f")
fams <- nat_pts |> transmute(region = coalesce(unname(MAP_NAME[lab]), lab), lab,
                             fam = ifelse(inside, fam, "between"))
world <- ggplot2::map_data("world") |> filter(region != "Antarctica") |> left_join(fams, by = "region")
base_map <- function(xlim, ylim, labels, lab_size = 3.6) {
  ggplot(world, aes(long, lat, group = group)) +
    geom_polygon(aes(fill = fam), colour = NIGHT, linewidth = 0.15) +
    # labels with a dark halo, pushed off the small countries with a leader line
    geom_text_repel(data = labels, aes(x, y, label = lab), inherit.aes = FALSE, family = "Inter", fontface = "bold",
                    size = lab_size, colour = INK, bg.color = NIGHT, bg.r = 0.15, min.segment.length = 0,
                    segment.colour = INK, segment.size = 0.3, box.padding = 0.2, point.padding = 0, seed = 3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = map_fill, labels = fam_lab, na.value = "#2b2f38",
                      breaks = names(fam_lab)) +
    coord_quickmap(xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim, expand = FALSE) +
    theme_void() + theme(legend.position = "none", plot.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA))
}
# label positions (longitude, latitude), placed by hand where the country is large enough
lab_world <- tribble(~lab, ~x, ~y,
  "United States", -100, 39, "Brazil", -52, -10, "Australia", 134, -25, "India", 79, 22, "Japan", 150, 36,
  "Nigeria", 8, 9.5, "Afghanistan", 66, 34, "Russia", 95, 62, "Fiji", 170, -17)
lab_eu <- tribble(~lab, ~x, ~y,
  "United Kingdom", -2.5, 53.5, "France", 2.5, 46.6, "Spain", -3.7, 40.2, "Italy", 12.6, 42.6,
  "Germany", 10.4, 51, "Belgium", 4.6, 50.6, "Switzerland", 8.2, 46.85, "Sweden", 15.5, 62.5,
  "Finland", 26, 63.5, "Serbia", 20.9, 44, "Romania", 25, 45.9, "Albania", 20, 41.1, "Turkey", 34, 39,
  "Morocco", -6.5, 31.5, "Algeria", 2.8, 28)
# Fiji is too small to see: a ring shows where it is
fiji_ring <- annotate("point", x = 178.5, y = -17.8, shape = 21, size = 4, colour = map_fill[["origin"]], stroke = 1)
p_world <- base_map(c(-170, 180), c(-48, 75), lab_world) + fiji_ring
p_eu <- base_map(c(-16, 50), c(27, 66), lab_eu)
# the key, in two columns under the maps
key <- tibble(fam = names(fam_lab), x = c(0, 0, 1, 1), y = c(0, -1, 0, -1)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = fam), shape = 15, size = 5.5) +
  geom_text(aes(x = x + 0.05, label = fam_lab[fam]), hjust = 0, family = "Inter", size = 4.1, colour = INK) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = map_fill, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.03, 1.9)) + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-1.5, 0.5)) + theme_void()
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 4.2
# GDP per capita (World Bank, 2023) against the compliments of the seven AIs; analysis/wealth.py
wealth <- read.csv(file.path("..", "analysis", "out", "wealth_by_country.csv")) |>
  left_join(nat_pts |> transmute(country, lab, fam = ifelse(inside, fam, "between")), by = "country")
w_rho <- read.csv(file.path("..", "analysis", "out", "wealth_spearman.csv"))
rho <- function(k) num(w_rho$rho[w_rho$measure == k], 2)
ggplot(wealth, aes(gdp_pc, compliment)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, colour = MUTED, fill = GRID, linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = fam), size = 3.6) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = lab, colour = fam), family = "Inter", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5, seed = 2,
                  box.padding = 0.3, min.segment.length = 0.3, segment.colour = "#55585f", bg.color = NIGHT, bg.r = 0.12) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = map_fill, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(500, 1000, 3000, 10000, 30000, 100000),
                labels = c("$500", "$1k", "$3k", "$10k", "$30k", "$100k")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, " %")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 41)) +
  labs(x = "GDP per person, 2023 (log scale)", y = "answers complimenting his culture") +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 11))
```

```{=latex}
\vspace{0.2em}
% the three correlations with GDP per person, Spearman over the 24 nationalities
\newcommand{\rhochip}[3]{\begin{tcolorbox}[enhanced, colback=panel, frame hidden, borderline north={3pt}{0pt}{#1}, arc=3pt, halign=center, top=5pt, bottom=5pt, left=4pt, right=4pt]
  {\fontsize{24}{26}\selectfont\bfseries\color{#1}#2\par}\vspace{0.1em}{\fontsize{10.5}{13}\selectfont\color{fg}#3\par}\end{tcolorbox}}
\begin{tcbraster}[raster columns=3, raster column skip=8pt, raster equal height]
\rhochip{green}{+`r rho("compliment")`}{compliments\\ on his culture}
\rhochip{heat}{`r sub("-", "−", rho("defensive"))`}{"his origin\\ does not matter"}
\rhochip{amber}{`r sub("-", "−", rho("risk"))`}{a risk tied\\ to his origin}
\end{tcbraster}
{\fontsize{11}{14}\selectfont\color{dim}Correlation with his country's wealth, from −1 to +1 (Spearman, 24 nationalities, all p < 0.001). Strong, but it does not prove a cause: wealth also goes with region, religion and how the news talk about these countries.\par}
{\fontsize{10}{13}\selectfont\color{dim}\faDatabase\enspace\textbf{Source:} World Bank, GDP per capita in current US\$, 2023 (indicator NY.GDP.PCAP.CD), \href{https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/NY.GDP.PCAP.CD}{\color{linkblue}\underline{data.worldbank.org}}, CC BY 4.0.\par}
\newpage
```

```{r}
tip <- tibble(x = c(-1.3, -0.6, 0, 0.7, 1.4), y = c(0, 0.8, 1.35, 0.75, 0))
body <- tibble(x = c(-1.3, -3.7, -4.5, -3.3, 0, 3.5, 4.6, 3.6, 1.4), y = c(0, -1.0, -3.0, -5.0, -5.6, -4.9, -2.9, -0.9, 0))
# what lies under the water: a coloured title and one line of detail each
under <- tibble(y = c(-0.95, -1.85, -2.75, -3.65, -4.55),
  title = c("\"his origin does not matter\"", "unequal compliments", "refusals to help", "a religion, a dress code",
            "nationality guessed"),
  detail = c(sprintf("%s of the answers", pc(p_def)),
             sprintf("Finland %s, Afghanistan %s", pc(sp_$p[sp_$country == "FIN"]), pc(sp_$p[sp_$country == "AFG"])),
             sprintf("up to %s for an Afghan man", pc(refu$p[refu$country == "AFG"], 1)),
             "his faith assumed, her clothes advised",
             sprintf("%s from the words alone (chance: 4 %%)", pc(g_acc))),
  col = c("#ff6a4d", "#2fbf8f", "#8b7cf0", "#eda100", "#5aa2ff"))
# the sea darkens with depth; the bands overlap a little, so that no thin line shows between them
water <- tibble(y0 = seq(0, -5.75, length.out = 40)) |> mutate(y1 = y0 - 5.75 / 40 - 0.03,
                                                              col = colorRampPalette(c("#173556", NIGHT))(40))
X0 <- -2.75
ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = water, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = y1, ymax = y0, fill = col), colour = NA) +
  geom_polygon(data = body, aes(x, y), fill = "#9fd3ff", alpha = 0.10, colour = "#5aa2ff", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_polygon(data = tip, aes(x, y), fill = "#eef6ff", colour = NA) +
  geom_polygon(data = tibble(x = c(0, 0.7, 1.4, 0.3), y = c(1.35, 0.75, 0, 0)), aes(x, y), fill = "#bcd9f5", colour = NA) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#8ec1ff", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("label", x = -4.85, y = 0.72, hjust = 0, family = "Inter", fontface = "bold", size = 4.0, lineheight = 0.95,
           colour = "white", fill = "#d63c2a", border.colour = "#d63c2a", label.r = unit(4, "pt"), label.padding = unit(4, "pt"),
           label = sprintf("What a quick test sees:\nexplicit risks (scams, migration),\n%s of the answers", pc(p_neg, 1))) +
  annotate("text", x = 4.9, y = -0.3, hjust = 1, family = "Inter", fontface = "bold", size = 3.9,
           colour = "#8ec1ff", label = "what this study adds ↓") +
  geom_point(data = under, aes(X0 - 0.3, y + 0.17, colour = col), size = 3.6) +
  geom_text(data = under, aes(X0, y + 0.17, label = title, colour = col), hjust = 0, family = "Inter",
            fontface = "bold", size = 4.6) +
  geom_text(data = under, aes(X0, y - 0.2, label = detail), hjust = 0, family = "Inter", size = 3.9, colour = INK) +
  scale_fill_identity() + scale_colour_identity() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-5, 5), ylim = c(-5.75, 1.5), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void()
```
